conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number found: guidance was reaffirmed unchanged on 2026-09-09, the bar ($1.84) sits a few cents above what the company's own guide arithmetic yields, and sector rotation has already taken the stock down 6% into the print; the findings roughly offset (sum -0.2) and p_up 48 on a 3.3% absolute move gives -0.13, both measurements agreeing that this is close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $1.84, revenue ~$258.7M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/INDB, read 2026-10-15) and $1.84 / ~$260.7-261.4M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/INDB/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet 2026-10-15). Two sources agree at $1.84; others disagree (sweep row's earlier EW read $1.81/$262M, StockAlarm $1.88 range $1.80-1.93, a July Chartmill figure of $1.93/$270.6M which is stale). Company guide (2026-09-09 Raymond James deck, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/776901/000077690126000140/investorpresentationslid.htm): Q4 2026 NIM 3.90-3.95% incl ~10bp accretion, core opex $553-557M FY plus $5-6M one-time core-system costs, tax 23.5-24.0%, stable asset quality. Q2 2026 actual: EPS $1.70 vs $1.77 consensus (miss).
positioning_check: Short interest ~2.1M shares, 4.5% of float, 5.1 days to cover, down 3.7% m/m (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/INDB, read 2026-10-15; settlement date not shown). Sweep row had 4.0% / 4.1 DTC (Equibles ~2026-08-19) and Benzinga 5.8% mid-September. Not crowded. No usable option chain (front expiry not two-sided, total OI 20, put/call OI 0.25), so no skew statement exists. Institutional flow labelled 'distributing' for the Sep 30 period (net -360K shares across 21 reporting funds). Tape: -6.21% over 20 days, -11.3% from 52w high, -5.8% since the July print per Earnings Whispers.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 (Raymond James conference, ~10 weeks into Q3) management reaffirmed every 2026 guidance line as 'No change': Q4 NIM target 3.90-3.95% incl ~0.10% accretion with 'consistent core margin expansion throughout 2026', explicitly 'neutral to any anticipated Federal Reserve action in 2026', core opex $553-557M plus $5-6M one-time conversion costs, tax 23.5-24.0%, 'stable asset quality metrics'. Q2 reported NIM was 3.85% (adjusted 3.76%), so the guide implies continued expansion; a mid-quarter reaffirmation lowers the odds of a large guide-down at the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (guidance held, EPS missed $1.70 vs $1.77) traded -3.05%; the last three prints were all negative (-3.05, -0.59, -2.76) and the name has not been rewarded for in-line guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public (8-K exhibit), so mostly priced; what is not priced is that the stock fell ~7% after the reaffirmation (from ~$83.4 on Sep 14 to $77.30) on sector flows rather than company news. If the market doubted the guide, analysts would have cut Q3 numbers below the guide arithmetic; instead consensus sits at or slightly above it.
findings.independence: Same document as the CRE office and pipeline findings (one deck, different slides). Q2 release (https://s206.q4cdn.com/952898466/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/INDB-2Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf) shows adjusted margin +4bp in Q2, consistent with the expansion path.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from the Q2 release plus the company guide puts Q3 EPS near $1.80-1.83, a few cents under the $1.84 consensus: Q2 NII $210.9M at 3.85% NIM (implied ~$22.0B earning assets), Q3 at ~3.88% and 92 days gives ~$216M NII; fees ~$42.5M (Q2 $42.4M) gives revenue ~$258-259M (EW consensus $258.7M, Benzinga ~$261M); H2 core opex implied by the $553-557M FY guide is ~$138-140M/qtr (H1 core ~$277M after removing $3.0M M&A and ~$3.2M one-time conversion costs) plus ~$1-2M of the remaining conversion costs; provision ~$6M; tax 23.75%; ~47.2M diluted shares if Q3 buybacks continued at Q2's ~$75M pace. Net income ~$85.5M / 47.2M = ~$1.81. Consensus needs either NIM at the high end already in Q3 or a lower provision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS miss of 7c (-4%) traded -3.05% next session; Q4 2025 print (2026-01-22) -2.76%; beats in 2025 traded +2.9% to +5.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference, not a document number; the bar is also disputed across providers ($1.81 to $1.88), so the market's own expectation is fuzzy. If the street had done this arithmetic, consensus would have drifted to ~$1.81 rather than sitting at $1.84 on two aggregators.
findings.independence: Uses the guide in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/776901/000077690126000140/investorpresentationslid018.jpg (shared with the guidance finding). Q2 itself missed consensus by 7c with $2.1M of one-time costs (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/INDB labels Q2 'Missed Consensus Estimates'). The buyback pace in Q3 is unsourced (no 8-K), which is the largest unknown in the share count.

findings.finding: Approved commercial pipeline at 2026-06-30 was $510M, up 62.9% from 3/31/26, after C&I grew $79.4M (+6.8% annualized) in Q2 net of $36.8M dealer-finance runoff; that pipeline funds in Q3, supporting loan growth against CRE/construction payoffs (-$176.4M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had total loans -0.2% despite C&I growth and the print traded -3.05%; loan growth has not been the line this stock moved on in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since the Q2 deck; lands inside the guide (C&I mid-single-digit growth, CRE flat to down), so it is mostly expected. What would differ if fully priced: consensus revenue would already embed loan growth, and the EW revenue figure ($258.7M) looks close to flat-balance-sheet arithmetic.
findings.independence: Same deck as the guidance finding. Q2 release (https://s206.q4cdn.com/952898466/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/INDB-2Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf) confirms C&I +1.7% QoQ and CRE -1.8%.

findings.finding: CRE office book ($1.024B, 10.9% of CRE) has $42.4M maturing in Q3 2026 of which $19.9M criticized, and $73.5M maturing in Q4 2026 of which $26.8M criticized and $17.4M classified; office nonperformers are $39.9M ($39.7M in top-20 borrowers). Total NPLs rose for a second straight quarter, $83.6M (Q4'25) to $96.6M to $103.6M (0.56% of loans), while the company guides 'stable asset quality'. A Q3 maturity resolved by charge-off or a Q4 classified loan moved to nonaccrual would land against the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 (a $54.6M Waltham office loan moved to nonperforming with a $22.4M reserve, per Banker & Tradesman 2024-10-18) is the closest precedent; the baseline does not attribute moves to lines. Q2 2026 NPL increase coincided with a -3.05% print.
findings.why_not_priced: The maturity schedule is in an 8-K exhibit slide that aggregators do not carry; consensus provision (~$6M implied) assumes no lumpy loss. If priced, the provision estimate would be higher or the stock would trade at a wider discount to TBV ($48.34 at 6/30; stock 1.6x TBV). Offset: criticized/classified commercial loans fell 5.2% in Q2 and NCOs were 2bp, so the trend is not one-directional.
findings.independence: Asset quality slide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/776901/000077690126000140/investorpresentationslid012.jpg, same deck) shows NPL trend; Q2 release shows provision $6.3M and NCOs $0.9M. Same company source throughout; no third-party credit event found (searched foreclosure/lawsuit news for Rockland Trust 2026: nothing).

findings.finding: Peer read, deposit costs: FB Financial (Oct 13, first-week Q3 reporter, Southeast) reported NIM down 12bp to 3.83% from 3.95% on 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields', total cost of deposits up to 2.32% from 2.26% on 'increased pricing on interest-bearing deposits', in a quarter where the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%. INDB's cost of deposits was flat at 1.36% in Q2 with 28% noninterest-bearing; deposit-cost creep would slow the NIM expansion the guide relies on.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy from a different region with a far higher deposit cost base (2.32% vs INDB 1.36%); macro-to-company transmission is not confirmed by INDB, which says its guide is neutral to Fed action. If priced, INDB consensus revenue would have been trimmed in October; EW's revenue figure is lower than the sweep's earlier read ($258.7M vs $262M), which may be partly that.
findings.independence: Fed hike confirmed at https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm. Counter-evidence filed separately (Home BancShares, funding costs falling).

findings.finding: Peer read, the other way: Home BancShares (Oct 14) reported NIM up 2bp to 4.53%, interest-bearing deposit rate down to 2.37% from 2.39%, interest expense down $2.3M, citing 'continued improvement in the Company's funding costs', with accretion lower; so the deposit-cost pressure at FB Financial is not universal among Q3 reporters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above; INDB's margin line moved the stock -3.05% on the Q2 mixed margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy; one day old, Arkansas-based. Market would price it into the group rather than INDB specifically.
findings.independence: Contradicts the FB Financial read (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm); together they net to roughly zero on peer funding costs.

findings.finding: The stock's drawdown into the print is sector flow, not company news: KBW Nasdaq Bank Index down 13% from mid-August as of 2026-10-02 and financials' worst month vs the S&P 500 since 1990, attributed by Truist's Brian Foran to rotation rather than results; INDB is -6.21% over 20 days and -5.8% since its July print (from ~$83.4 on Sep 14), with no company 8-K other than the dividend and the reaffirming deck. A print near the bar may let the stock recover toward its post-July VWAP (~$82).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline attributable; the run-up is negative into this print, unlike the Q2 setup.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly a positioning call; LESSONS rule 5 warns an unexplained drawdown is worth little, but this one has an explanation (sector flows) and no company-specific cause in the filings. If the market saw a company-specific problem, short interest would be rising; Equibles shows it down 3.7% m/m at 4.5% of float.
findings.independence: Institutional flow 'distributing' at Sep 30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/INDB) is consistent with sector outflows; Earnings Whispers post-July drift -5.8% (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/INDB).

findings.finding: Insiders were net sellers of ~$760.7K over the last 90 days with no buys; Forms 144 filed 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-25 and Forms 4 on 2026-08-05, 08-26 and 08-31; no insider buying into the drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and routine-sized; public in EDGAR. Would matter only if it were a cluster by senior officers, which the amounts do not suggest.

findings.finding: Core system upgrade is scheduled for October 2026 (deck slide 'Near-Term Priorities'); $3.2M of the $5-6M guided one-time costs were booked in H1 (Q1 ~$1.1M, Q2 $2.1M), leaving ~$1.8-2.8M for H2, most likely Q3/Q4, and the call on 2026-10-16 will be the first read on how the conversion went.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 included $2.1M of these costs and missed by 7c; the costs themselves were disclosed and inside guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance, so priced; filed because a conversion problem disclosed on the call would land inside the window. No customer-facing disruption found (searched Rockland Trust conversion 2026: only the October 2025 Enterprise conversion notices).
findings.independence: Q2 release confirms the $2.1M one-time cost (https://s206.q4cdn.com/952898466/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/INDB-2Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf).

baseline_tension: No skew exists to agree or disagree with; the findings net slightly negative on the number (bar a few cents above guide arithmetic) and slightly positive on positioning (a sector-flow drawdown of -6% into the print), consistent with a near-zero call and with the name's habit of selling its prints.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the guidance-reaffirmation and commercial-pipeline findings both land inside what the company guided, trimmed +0.3 to +0.2 each; the core-conversion one-off is inside the $5-6M guided cost, -0.1 to 0.0.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is now sourced to two agreeing aggregators at $1.84, but other providers range $1.81-1.88, so the guide-arithmetic shortfall finding stays small, trimmed -0.5 to -0.4.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked (4.5% of float, 5.1 days, falling), not crowded, so the negative findings were not shrunk further; there is no skew to beat.

Rule 1 and the pessimism note: the name sold its last three prints, which keeps p_up just under 50 instead of pushing the positives larger; sum unchanged at -0.2 and the scaled number unchanged at -0.13.
